summary: Traced the follower-side protection behind the only execution-free account and recorded it: the AppendEntries conflict loop deletes from the first entry whose term differs through the follower's last index and then rewinds the latest configuration to the committed one exactly when that deletion covers the latest configuration index, while the committed configuration is only written by the append shortcut in processConfigurationLogEntry, a commit advance on either side, or a snapshot install. One new source anchor (raft.go 1955-1962), one new behavior knowledge entry citing the five relevant anchors, and the refuted question's discriminator re-pointed at the trace that would falsify it: a follower appending a configuration entry, never seeing it committed, then having it truncated by a new leader's conflicting AppendEntries. Validation returned valid with those three effects and no execution requested; incomplete work is that trace itself, which remains unmeasured, along with the assumption that no producer writes a second uncommitted configuration into a log.
